Bitcoin Miners Pay to Exit as Average Mining Cost Hits $75.5K per BTC CoinShares said listed Bitcoin miners fell below cash breakeven in aggregate in Q2 2026, with the weighted average pre-tax cash cost to produce one BTC reaching about $75,500, versus Bitcoin’s quarter-end price of $58,400. Monthly average hash price also fell to a record low of $27.7/PH/s/day in June. The pressure is pushing miners to scale back or exit, with Core Scientific paying $41.9 million to cancel roughly 15 EH/s of next-generation mining hardware, while several listed miners have already shut down or are winding down operations. — link

WSJ: Warsh Faces 90% Rate-Hike Odds as Trump-Fed Truce Comes Under Pressure Investors now see about a 90% chance that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will raise rates this week, putting his political truce with President Trump under its biggest test yet. Warsh took office after criticizing the Fed for cutting too slowly, but rising energy prices, new tariffs, AI-driven demand and a firmer August inflation print have sharply changed the backdrop. Trump spent much of last year pushing for lower rates, while White House adviser Kevin Hassett said the president would respect the Fed’s decision even though he would not be “super happy” about a hike. Wall Street Journal reporter Nick Timiraos said central-bank watchers now overwhelmingly expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates this week and then hike again before the end of 2026. Markets have already moved close to fully pricing in this week’s increase, with recent inflation and energy-price pressures reinforcing expectations that tightening may continue beyond September. — link

Highlight Clip: The US Allows Perps, but Onchain Perps Are Still a Different Matter The US Allows Perps, but Onchain Perps Are Still a Different Matter On September 7, 2026, Jake Chervinsky, CEO of the Hyperliquid Policy Center, said in an interview with The Rollup that the U.S. has allowed exchanges to offer bitcoin perpetuals, but onchain perps face a different regulatory challenge. He noted that the CFTC has approved Coinbase and Kraken to offer bitcoin perps, but the approvals still apply to traditional centralized exchanges, leaving permissionless blockchains like Hyperliquid without a clear compliance path. He said the key goal is to bring onchain markets into the U.S., rather than simply returning perpetuals to traditional market structures. — link

Republicans Reject Democrats’ CLARITY Act Counteroffer as 60-Vote Outcome Remains Uncertain According to Punchbowl News and Crypto In America, Senate Republicans rejected Democrats’ latest CLARITY Act counterproposal ahead of Tuesday’s 2:15 p.m. ET cloture vote, which requires 60 votes to advance. Democrats sought tighter ethics rules, narrower BRCA developer protections and stronger conflict-of-interest provisions, while leaving stablecoin yield largely unchanged. Republicans say their latest text already includes 126 substantive Democratic changes and call it their “last, best and final offer.” The vote count remains uncertain. — link
